title: On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres
author: Nicolaus Copernicus
description: Heliocentric model of the solar system that initiated the Scientific Revolution
rights: Public domain in the US. Charles Glenn Wallis (1914-1944) translated this while a tutor and editor at St John's College, Annapolis, where he oversaw cheap mimeographed editions of classical texts for classroom use; his Copernicus was published there by the St John's Bookstore in 1939. Published in the US before 1964 with copyright not renewed, so it is in the public domain — and a mimeographed bookstore edition may well have carried no notice at all, which would put it in the public domain by a second route. Verified 2026-08-25. SOURCE FILE CAVEAT, and it does not affect the published text: the PDF in this directory is a modern composite with no title or copyright page, and it appends Rheticus's Narratio Prima in what appears to be Edward Rosen's translation (Three Copernican Treatises, Columbia UP, 1939) whose renewal status we have NOT checked. The Narratio Prima is a separate 1540 work by another author and was stripped at extraction, so our markdown contains only Copernicus, from his dedication to Paul III onward. The question therefore attaches to the tracked source PDF, not to what we publish.
